references.text: The ark is called the 'ark of the testimony' because it contains the testimony (the tablets of the law) that God gave to Moses.
The description of how the veil was to be made, with cherubim woven into it, hanging on four pillars.
Moses receives the command to place the ark of the testimony in the tabernacle and shield it with the veil.
Fulfillment of the command: Moses placed the ark in the tabernacle and hung up the covering veil to shield it.
The veil separates the Most Holy Place where the mercy seat above the ark is, and only the high priest could enter there.
The priests carried the ark of the covenant into the inner room of the temple, the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the cherubim.
Hope as an anchor for the soul, which enters within the veil, where Jesus entered as a forerunner.
Hebrews describes the second veil that separated the holy place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark stood.
At Jesus' death, the temple veil was torn in two from top to bottom, symbolizing free access to God.
Clarifies the space between the altar and the Most Holy Place by placing the incense altar before the separating veil.
Complementary descriptions of the Most Holy Place: the contents of the ark and its placement behind the veil.
Explains the consequence of the veil as a divider: only priests have access to the service within.
Defines a coherent spatial division: the table of showbread outside versus the ark behind the veil.
